regions.summary: Commented code: DecodeNametableList, Nt_DecodeTileBlock, Nt_DecodeAttrBlock, Nt_QueueRowHeader, Nt_ReadRecord, Nt_StartBlock ...

units.name: DecodeNametableList
units.summary: Draw a list of compressed nametable blocks (called through DecodeNametableFar with banks 4/5 mapped). List at (Temp6): records "step, vram lo, vram hi, src lo, src hi", terminated by a zero step. Step 8 marks an attribute-table block (also mirrored into AttrShadowNt0). Each block is decompressed row by row into PPU queue commands, waiting for a frame (or flushing) after every row.

units.name: Nt_DecodeTileBlock
units.summary: Decode one block: first two decoded bytes are row count and width; every further byte is XOR-chained with the previous one (delta coding) and queued.

units.name: Nt_DecodeAttrBlock
units.summary: As Nt_DecodeTileBlock, also storing each byte into AttrShadowNt0.

units.name: Nt_QueueRowHeader
units.summary: Queue "set address VramPtr; copy Temp1 inline bytes"; Temp2 = byte count.

units.name: Nt_ReadRecord
units.summary: Read a list record: VramStep, VramPtr and SrcPtr.

units.name: Nt_StartBlock
units.summary: Reset the decoder state and read the block header (rows -> Temp0, width -> Temp1).

units.name: Nt_NextByte
units.summary: Return the next decompressed byte. A flag byte (Temp8) supplies one bit per output byte: 0 = literal from the stream, 1 = repeat the run value (Temp3) when the second flag byte (Temp9) also says so. Group headers are refilled every 8/64 bytes.

units.name: Nt_AdvanceCounters
units.summary: Advance the nametable decoder position; every 64 bytes start a new group.

units.name: Nt_ReadGroupHeader
units.summary: Read a group header: a zero byte introduces a new run value (Temp3) and flag byte.

units.summary: Start animation A for object X: look up AnimScriptTable[A] (at $81FA), reset base tile, delay and loop counter, and mark the animation running (Var0461 bit 6).

units.name: Anim_RunScript
units.summary: Count down the frame delay; when it expires interpret the animation script until a frame command. Bytes >= $C0 are commands (AnimCommandTable), others are frames: tile offset (bit 7 = flipped) followed by a delay. Returns carry set with AnimTile when a new frame was selected.

units.name: LoadSpritePaletteFromPtr

units.name: QueueFillRow
units.summary: Append "set address VramPtr; fill Temp1 bytes with Temp3" to the PPU queue.

units.name: DrawWindowFrame
units.summary: Queue a bordered window, one row per frame. Temp0 = height in rows, Temp1 = width; VramPtr = top-left nametable address. The first row uses border tiles 1/2/3, middle rows 4/space/5 and the last row 6/7/8, each emitted as queue commands (address, literal, fill-run, literal).

units.name: AdvanceSrcPtrByY
units.summary: Add Y to SrcPtr and reset Y to 0 (keeps (SrcPtr),y reads within range).

units.name: AdvanceVramPtrRow
units.summary: Add VramStep to VramPtr (move to the next nametable row).

units.name: DecodeNametableFar
units.summary: Map banks 4/5 and call the compressed-nametable decoder at bank 4 $8000 (argument list pointer in Temp6/Temp7), then restore the previous PRG banks.

units.name: PpuQueue_Reset
units.summary: Empty the PPU queue (index 0 and an end marker at PpuQueue[0]).

units.name: PpuQueue_Execute
units.summary: NMI-time interpreter for the PPU command queue at PpuQueue. Banks 4/5 are mapped while it runs because queue commands 3 and 5 may point at data there. Stream format (Y = read index): byte >= $20 : literal tile, written to PPUDATA $00 end      $01 lo,hi set VRAM address   $02 b write one byte (escape) $03 n,ptr    copy n bytes from ptr        $04 n,bytes copy n inline bytes $05 ptr      copy zero-t
